issues.legal_issue: A High Court should not express a view on the merits of a land-grabbing order after indicating that the affected parties may pursue other remedies, where that merits view could predetermine those remedies.
material_facts: The High Court indicated that the appellants could seek review of the Special Court’s order and pursue a suit concerning title and rights.
The High Court also approved the Special Court’s decision on the merits.
The Supreme Court considered that the High Court’s merits view could make the outcome of a subsequent review or suit a foregone conclusion.
issues.conclusion: The orders confirming the Special Court’s decision were set aside, and the writ petition was restored and remitted to the High Court for fresh decision without the Supreme Court expressing any view on the merits.
issues.legal_principle: When a court identifies remedies that remain available to parties, it should not also express a merits opinion that could prejudge those remedies. The Supreme Court applied this principle in the context of the review remedy under Section 17-A of the Andhra Pradesh Land Grabbing (Prohibition) Act, 1982.

predicates.challenge_to_land_grabbing_order: The proceeding challenges an order made in a land-grabbing matter.
predicates.alternative_remedies_identified: The reviewing court indicates that the affected parties may pursue other remedies concerning the order or their rights.
predicates.merits_view_expressed: The reviewing court expresses approval or disapproval of the merits in a way that could predetermine the outcome of those other remedies.

issues.definition: When a challenge to a land-grabbing order is heard, other remedies are identified, and a potentially prejudicial merits view is expressed, that view should be set aside and the case reconsidered without prejudgment.

issues.legal_issue: A civil court cannot entertain a suit for title concerning land alleged to have been grabbed when the matter falls within the jurisdiction of the special land-grabbing court.
material_facts: The dispute concerned land alleged to have been grabbed and was the subject of a proceeding before the Special Court.
The High Court had suggested that the appellants could file a civil suit for a declaration of title and rights.

The Supreme Court held that a suit concerning title to the disputed land could not be entertained by a civil court, having regard to the statutory provisions governing the Special Court and the transfer of matters within its jurisdiction.
issues.conclusion: A civil suit for title concerning the land alleged to have been grabbed would not be maintainable.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 8(2) and 15 of the Andhra Pradesh Land Grabbing (Prohibition) Act, 1982, a civil court cannot entertain a title suit concerning land alleged to have been grabbed where the matter is within the Special Court’s jurisdiction. Section 8(8) provides for the transfer to the Special Court of pending matters that would fall within its jurisdiction.

predicates.civil_title_suit: The proceeding is a civil suit seeking a determination of title to land.
predicates.land_is_alleged_to_have_been_grabbed: The land in the suit is alleged to have been grabbed.
predicates.matter_within_special_court_jurisdiction: The dispute falls within the jurisdiction assigned to a special court for land-grabbing matters.

issues.definition: A civil title suit concerning land alleged to have been grabbed must not be entertained when the dispute falls within the special court’s jurisdiction.
